app.name: Code Graph
app.description: Multi-language code analysis system based on tree-sitter

args.refresh_all: Incremental refresh code graph (only parse changed files, no data wiped)
args.force: Force reparse all files (ignore incremental build)
args.topo_limit: Number of topo sorted items to show
args.file: Get all symbols in a file
args.history: View all historical versions of a function
args.restore_all_comments: Batch restore comments for all functions with history
args.restore_file: Only restore comments for specified file (with --restore-all-comments)
args.preview: Preview restore result (don't write to file)
args.uncommented: List uncommented symbols (default: fn, optional: struct/enum/trait)
args.uncommented_module: Module filter for uncommented symbols (prefix match)
args.search_kind: Filter search results by symbol kind
args.impact: Impact analysis: trace upstream functions that call this function
args.call_chain: Call chain down: trace downstream functions called by this function
args.orphan_symbols: Uncalled orphan symbols (default: fn, optional: struct/enum/trait)
args.orphan_module: Module filter for orphan symbols (prefix match)
args.deepest: Deepest call depth functions ranking (default: top 20)
args.export_module_graph: Export module dependency graph (mermaid or dot, default: mermaid)
args.graph_output: Output file path for module graph
args.call_heatmap: Function call frequency heatmap (module or file, default: module)
args.function_issues: Detect function issues (missing comments/hardcoded/TODO/unwrap/etc.), optionally specify function name
args.semgrep_save: Save Semgrep scan results to database
args.issue_module: Module filter for issue detection (prefix match)
args.semgrep_config: Semgrep ruleset config (default: p/default, e.g. p/security, p/best-practices)
args.git_import: Import Git history (optionally max commits, default 100)
args.git_show: Show change details for a specific commit
args.largest_fns: Show largest functions by line count (default 20)
args.fn_metrics: Show detailed metrics for a function
args.embed: Generate vector embeddings for all functions
args.similar: Find functions similar to the specified one
args.install_lang: Only install specified language grammars (e.g. csharp ruby)
args.install_check: Only check dependency status, do not install

task_constraints_annotate: Only add comments; do not change function logic
Use the target language's comment style (Rust: /// or /** */, Python: # or docstring)
task_constraints_refactor: Keep external behavior unchanged (signature, return value, side effects)
Update callers when public API changes are involved
task_constraints_fix: Fix only the reported issue; avoid unrelated changes
The previous check gate must pass after the fix
task_constraints_edit: Use propose_edit for writes; do not write directly to the filesystem
Run dry_run first to inspect the diff
Provide expected_hash to prevent concurrent overwrite

messages.install_agent_skill_md:
---
name: callwarden-workflow
description: Use Call Warden for codebase-aware tasks in large or risky repositories. Trigger for bugfixes, refactors, code review, annotation, broad edits, impact analysis, or any task touching more than one file or more than a few steps.
---

Use the Call Warden MCP server as the primary workflow entrypoint.

1. Prefer `work_next_job` over manual file search when a task_id exists.
2. Prefer `file_symbol_content` / symbol-context tools over whole-file reads.
3. Prefer `propose_symbol_patch` or `propose_range_patch` over whole-file rewrites.
4. For broad tasks, create/split tasks first, then repeatedly call `work_next_job`.
5. After editing, report the step with `task_report_step` and include changed files.
6. Do not run destructive git commands such as `git reset --hard`, `git checkout .`, or `git clean -fd`.
messages.install_agent_cursor_rule:
---
description: Call Warden workflow for codebase-aware Agent tasks
alwaysApply: true
---

When the Call Warden MCP server is available, prefer it for broad or risky coding tasks.

- Use `work_next_job` for task-driven work instead of manually deciding the next file.
- Use symbol/range patch tools instead of full-file rewrites.
- Use Call Warden impact and guardrail tools before DB/API/config changes.
- Avoid destructive git cleanup commands unless the user explicitly requests them.
messages.install_agent_readme:
# Call Warden {agent} integration

This directory contains generated integration files for {agent}.

Recommended workflow:

1. Enable the MCP server config that points to `python cw.py server`.
2. Enable the generated skill/rule instructions.
3. Enable hooks where the target Agent supports them.
4. For large tasks, ask the Agent to start from Call Warden `work_next_job`.

The hook script blocks destructive git cleanup commands and refreshes the graph after edits when the Agent exposes edited file paths in hook payloads.

Before editing code, AI agents should:
1. Prefer small files; split large files before editing when possible
2. Understand complex functions fully, or split them first
3. Validate all call sites after editing highly coupled modules
4. Refactor before editing functions over 200 lines or complexity > 30

- Logic errors because complex functions are easy to break
Recommendation: split into smaller files/functions, then edit incrementally

cli.subcommand_help:
Code Warden Architecture Subcommands (Four Pillars):

  Guardrail:
    guardrail scan [--file <path>] [--category <cat>]   Scan guardrail violations
    guardrail rules [--category <cat>]                  List guardrail rules

  Change Impact:
    impact <symbol_hash> [--depth N]                    Compute change impact radius
    review <symbol_hash>                                Generate review readiness report

  Evolution Intelligence:
    evolution <qualified_name> [--window 30d]           Query function change frequency
    hotspot [--module <path>]                           Hotspot function ranking
    churn [--module <path>] [--window 90d]              Code churn analysis

  Defect Knowledge Base:
    defect search [--category <cat>] [--severity <sev>] Search defect patterns
    defect suggest <symbol_hash> [--finding <id>]       Recommend fix suggestions
    defect learn <commit_hash>                          Learn from fix commit
    defect stats                                        Defect KB statistics
    defect build                                        Build defect knowledge base

  Code Graph GC (Java-like GC, archive files hit by .gitignore/.callwardenignore):
    gc archive [--force] [--dry-run]                    Archive files hit by ignore rules
    gc restore [--path <path> ...] [--force]            Restore archived files
    gc status                                           View GC status (active/archived/deleted stats)
    gc purge [--older-than <days>]                      Permanently remove files archived over N days

  Diagnostics & Maintenance:
    doctor                                              Check environment, database status, recommended optimizations
    doctor --add-defender-exclusion                     Add Windows Defender exclusion (requires admin privileges)

Legacy Commands (--flag mode):
  The following options are legacy --flag style commands, coexisting with the above subcommands.
